# Task P6-04: Import-list providers — Last.fm, ListenBrainz, and a reference library as a list

**Phase:** 6 · **Depends on:** P6-01 (merged) · **Suggested tier:** T2 worker · **Estimated size:** M

## Goal

More list sources (ADR-0012): a user's **Last.fm** loved or top tracks, a user's **ListenBrainz** loved tracks or one ListenBrainz playlist, and a **reference library** read as a list (its identified files in folder order — so a DJ set or a curated folder becomes a playlist). Each provider only reads its source and returns `ImportListEntry` rows in order; the sync (P6-01) resolves and adds, P6-03 writes playlists. No UI, no migration.

## Deliverables

### 1. HTTP

- One named `HttpClient` per service, registered next to the other metadata clients (read `src/Wondarr.Core/Metadata/MetadataServiceCollectionExtensions.cs` and copy how the LRCLIB or Deezer client is registered: base address, `User-Agent` from the same options, the standard resilience/timeout setup): `lastfm` (`https://ws.audioscrobbler.com/2.0/`) and `listenbrainz` (`https://api.listenbrainz.org/1/`).
- **A non-JSON answer is a failure, never an empty list.** ListenBrainz sometimes answers HTTP 200 with an HTML "Verifying your browser" page (fixture `tests/fixtures/listenbrainz/browser-check.html`, recorded 2026-10-07). Check the `Content-Type`/first character and fail the read with "ListenBrainz asked for a browser check; the list will be read again later." Same idea for Last.fm.
- Rate limits: ListenBrainz sends `X-RateLimit-Remaining` / `X-RateLimit-Reset-In` (limit 30); when `Remaining` is 0 wait `Reset-In` seconds (max 60) before the next page. A 429 fails the read with a "try later" message. Last.fm: at most 5 requests per second (a simple delay between pages is enough); error code 29 → "try later".
- Never log the Last.fm API key; it is a `Secret` field (masked by the API already, P6-01).

### 2. Providers (`src/Wondarr.Core/ImportLists/LastFm/`, `ListenBrainz/`, `References/`)

- `LastFmLovedProvider` (`Type = "lastfmLoved"`, "Last.fm loved tracks"): fields `user` (text, required), `apiKey` (password, required, `Secret: true`; help: "Your own Last.fm API key, from last.fm/api/account/create"). `GET ?method=user.getlovedtracks&user=…&api_key=…&format=json&limit=200&page=N` until `page >= @attr.totalPages` (max 50 pages). Each `lovedtracks.track[]`: `name`, `artist.name`, `mbid` (often empty — treat `""` as null). Entry `ExternalId: "lastfm:" + lowercase(artist) + "|" + lowercase(name)`.
- `LastFmTopProvider` (`Type = "lastfmTop"`, "Last.fm top tracks"): fields `user`, `apiKey` (as above), `period` (select: `overall`, `7day`, `1month`, `3month`, `6month`, `12month`; default `12month`), `count` (number 1–500, default 50). `method=user.gettoptracks&period=…&limit=min(count,200)` paged until `count` rows. `toptracks.track[]` adds `duration` (seconds, as a string; `"0"` = unknown) → `DurationMs`.
- Last.fm errors are `{"error": N, "message": "…"}` (6 = user not found, 10/26 = bad key, 29 = rate limit): map to `Failed("Last.fm: <message>")`, without the key.
- `ListenBrainzLovedProvider` (`Type = "listenbrainzLoved"`, "ListenBrainz loved tracks"): field `user`. `GET feedback/user/{user}/get-feedback?score=1&count=100&offset=N&metadata=true` until `offset >= total_count` (max 100 pages). Entry: `ExternalId: "lb:" + recording_mbid`, `MbRecordingId: recording_mbid`, `Title: track_metadata.track_name`, `Artist: track_metadata.artist_name`. A row without `recording_mbid` uses its `recording_msid` for the id and no MBID.
- `ListenBrainzPlaylistProvider` (`Type = "listenbrainzPlaylist"`, "ListenBrainz playlist"): field `playlist` (text, required: `https://listenbrainz.org/playlist/{mbid}` or the bare MBID). `GET playlist/{mbid}` → JSPF `playlist.track[]`: `title`, `creator`, `album`, `duration` (ms), `identifier` (a list of `https://musicbrainz.org/recording/{mbid}` — take the first recording MBID). Entry `ExternalId: "lb:" + mbid` (or `"lb:" + position` when a track has none). 404 → `Failed("The ListenBrainz playlist was not found, or it is private.")`.
- `ReferenceLibraryListProvider` (`Type = "referenceLibrary"`, "Reference library"): field `referenceLibraryId` (number, required; `Validate` checks it is a positive integer — it cannot reach the database, so existence is checked in `FetchAsync`). `FetchAsync` reads the reference library's files that are identified (`ReferenceFile.SongId != null`), ordered by `RelativePath` (ordinal, case-insensitive), joined to their songs: entry `ExternalId: "ref:" + file id`, `MbRecordingId`, `Artist` (`song.ArtistCredit`), `Title`, `DurationMs`. A missing library → `Failed("Reference library N does not exist.")`. Inject `WondarrDbContext` (register this provider **scoped**). The song a reference file is identified as already exists, so the sync links the item to it ("already in the library") — the point of this list is its order and its playlist.
- All five registered as **scoped** `IImportListProvider` in `src/Wondarr.Core/ServiceCollectionExtensions.cs` next to the CSV provider.

### 3. Tests

- `tests/Wondarr.Core.Tests/ImportLists/ListenBrainzProvidersTests.cs`: loved (`tests/fixtures/listenbrainz/feedback-loved-p0.json`: `count` 3, `total_count` 244 — make the stub answer page 2 with an empty `feedback` and `total_count` 3 to stop; first entry recording `e53766ad-b80e-40ab-b28c-a2f0a1aa414e`, "Y4R4", "Seren Saraç"); playlist (`playlist-34c1bb9f.json`: 3 tracks, the first "Imagine" by A Perfect Circle, 296 000 ms, recording `f99c04dc-9f75-4af8-bdf8-465c40c18822`); the browser-check page → failure with the "try later" message; a playlist link parsed to its MBID. Use a stub `HttpMessageHandler` (find the one the existing metadata or LRCLIB tests use and reuse it).
- `tests/Wondarr.Core.Tests/ImportLists/LastFmProvidersTests.cs`: hand-written JSON in the documented shape (`{"lovedtracks":{"track":[{"name":"Get Lucky","mbid":"","artist":{"name":"Daft Punk","mbid":"…"}}],"@attr":{"page":"1","totalPages":"1","perPage":"200","total":"1","user":"x"}}}`, and `toptracks` with `"duration":"369"`), paging over two pages, an error body (`{"error":6,"message":"User not found"}`) → failure without the key in the message, `count` and `period` validation, the key never appearing in a logged or returned string.
- `tests/Wondarr.Core.Tests/ImportLists/ReferenceLibraryListProviderTests.cs`: a SQLite test database (see `ImportListServiceTests` for the setup) with a reference library, three files (two identified, one not) → two entries in path order with their MBIDs; an unknown id fails.
- `tests/Wondarr.Api.Tests/ImportListApiTests.cs`: extend the schema test to list the five new types (that file is in scope for this assertion only).

## Constraints

- A provider only reads; never resolve, add or delete.
- Never log or return the Last.fm API key; never log request URLs that carry it.
- Workers cannot set environment variables in commands: do **not** try to regenerate `docs/api/openapi.json` (this task adds no endpoint anyway).
- Build after adding new test files before running tests.
